text:
SILENT NIGHT
Early in the second half of Tuesday night’s National League South match between Torquay United and Chesham, play was briefly suspended due to an ear-splitting din emitted over the Plainmoor public address system. “The game has stopped because the Torquay Tannoy system is making a loud noise that won’t stop,” posted Chesham on their Social Media Disgrace account. “I’m not kidding.” A sort of aural cross between an ocean liner’s foghorn and a party conference speech delivered by a senior member of the Reform party, it eventually stopped and play resumed with Torquay running out 2-1 winners.
At the same time around 420km north of Devon, the players of Manchester City and Napoli were playing out a 2-2 draw in comparative silence, as an eerily quiet home crowd watched their once all-conquering side extend their winless run to five matches and fail to keep a clean sheet for the 10th game in a row. While it is fair to say their performance against the Italian side was significantly better than the shift they put in against Fulham on Saturday, the bar is currently so low that even a snake would struggle to limbo beneath it. “Football is easy and difficult,” sighed Erling Haaland, who looked mightily fed up at having gone three consecutive City games without scoring a goal. “When you win it’s easy and you know what to do. When you don’t you start questioning everything. The perfect thing would be to not think but it’s not so easy.”
His teammate Rayan Cherki, who scored City’s equaliser with one of his trademark soft-shoe shuffles, was considerably less equanimous. “I don’t care about my goal,” he harrumphed at his inquisitor. “I wanted to win the game. Sometimes the game is not like you want and today is like the last game, the last two or three games. We need to work more and come back for a win, just that.” Dressed in what looked like an American prison issue-style orange fourth strip their club introduced as “a special edition kit in collaboration with Puma and CP Company”, the duo cut disconsolate figures before being led away to await whatever sentence is handed down to their club on the back of those guilty verdicts for breaching Premier League rules, though the club is appealing.
With money tight and the weather baltic, it was no surprise there were plenty of midweek no-shows and the sheer volume of unsold tickets did not go unnoticed by gleeful online Etihad Stadium seat scrutineers. Large sections of the stadium’s upper tier were left unopened on a night the fans who did turn up reserved their loudest cheers and a bespoke tifo for their returning hero Kevin De Bruyne. It suggested the Belgium midfielder is more popular at his former club than the one he now plays for. Before the match, De Bruyne said his feelings for City “will never change” even if they end up being stripped of all the Premier League titles he won with them. Given his apparent dissatisfaction at Napoli and rumours of a January exit, the 35-year-old could always re-sign for City and play out his dotage in the noisy surroundings of the North West Counties League.
LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE
The Bigger Cup action continues this evening: Rob Smyth brings you live updates on Sporting 1-1 Manchester United at 8pm GMT, while at the same time Simon Burnton will be following Club Brugge 0-2 Liverpool and the rest of the night’s action at the same in his clockwatch.
QUOTE OF THE DAY
“I can see the team is in a difficult moment but I have already watched many of the games over the last few days and I’m very confident about the future” – Edward Iordanescu is the latest man to be given a crack at the Watford job. He’s their sixth head coach in less than 18 months and the 25th since the Pozzo family took control of the Hornets in 2012. That is more than Liverpool have had in their entire history dating back to 1892.
FOOTBALL DAILY LETTERS
 In this constantly changing world of global disruptions, uncertainties and risks, with social, political and economic disaffection seemingly on the rise everywhere, it’s genuinely heartening to know that some things never change. ‘Plus ça change, plus c’est la même chose’, as the late, great French writer Jean-Baptiste Alphonse Karr famously said, something that I’m sure Big Dunc is well aware of” – Noble Francis.
 May I be the 1,092nd correspondent to demand a review of the Letter o’ the Day award for Monday – and it be awarded to Declan Hackett for his letter foretelling the rescinding of the red card given to Lenny Yoro on Sunday? Given the precedent of awarding/revoking/re-awarding of the Afcon 2025 edition this would be entirely justified” – Peter Martin.
If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Rollover. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, are here.

digest_he: מנצ'סטר סיטי נפרדה בתיקו שני מול נאפולי לעיני קהל ביתי שקט באצטדיון איתיחאד, והאריכה בכך את רצף המשחקים ללא ניצחון לחמישה משחקים רצופים, וכן נכשלה בשמירה על רשת נקייה במשך עשרה משחקים. החלוץ ארלינג האלאנד הביע תסכול מהמצב המקצועי המורכב, וכך גם חברו לקבוצה רייאן שרקי. במקביל, הקבוצה ממשיכה להתמודד עם השלכות משפטיות וחקירות סביב הפרות לכאורה של חוקי הפרמייר ליג, בעוד המאמן והשחקנים מנסים לייצב את השורות לקראת המשך העונה המסובכת.
